sections.text: Surely wisdom is like the sun, revealing the supreme truth to those whose ignorance is dispelled by the wisdom of the Self.
Meditating on the Divine, having faith in the Divine, concentrating on the Divine and losing themselves in the Divine, their sins dissolved in wisdom, they go whence there is no return.
Sages look equally upon all, whether he be a minister of learning and humility, or an infidel, or whether it be a cow, an elephant or a dog.

We had been discussing chapter five, Karma Sannyasa Yoga. So far we have seen that Bhagavan said Karma Yoga is clearly better for you, because Sannyasa may be more difficult to pursue for one who has not developed the quality of na dveshti na kankshati -- who does not hate or does not even desire. For such a person, Sannyasa is not really easy to practice.
Therefore, Karma Yoga -- Yoga Yukta Bhava, become Yoga Yukta. Yoga Yukta Bhava is to develop the art of performing actions for the greater good, not for myself. And the technique given to us in this chapter says: while you are performing all your actions, constantly think that you are not doing anything. Pralapan, vishrujan, srunan, svashan -- even when you are breathing, seeing, hearing, touching, think that you are not doing that. Someone other than what you think you are is doing it.
So thats the technique given to us: constantly, while Im acting in this world, I should see that something else is doing it. What is that something else? Well, we can clearly identify that everything we do is either my body doing it, my mind doing it, or my intellect doing it. The observer who is observing this activity is someone other than body, mind, and intellect. So constantly see yourself as the witness of your own activity. Just as when we witness other people and say, I know hes doing well, hes not doing well, I think hes wrong or hes right -- but we are not involved in it. We are constantly judging other people from our vantage point, our perspective.
If we start developing a practice where we can do the same thing for ourselves, we will clearly see what is right and wrong for us. When we do something wrong, if we step out of that activity and see it, well see whether that was right or wrong, and the next time we can correct it. So the technique is given to us: constantly watch yourself as a third-party observer in all the activities you do.
And then the last few verses we had been discussing, where Bhagavan comes out and says Nakartrutvam lokasya Prabhu -- the Lord is not creating any sense of doership.
The ego which I have right now saying this is me and I am the doer. I am the enjoyer and I am the sufferer. Bhagawan said, I really have nothing to do with it. So please dont blame me. I did not create this ego for you. It is the very part of the Prakriti that these activities are going on.
Your body, mind and intellect are nothing but part of the Prakriti. You identifying it created this ego. But I am not the creator of your ego. You now have the responsibility to get rid of the ego yourself. Nakartruttam na karmanis Lokas. The Lord who is the Lord of my being is not responsible or not the creator of this ego.
That sense of this is me, thats not me, nobody else could have done it without me, this cannot function without me -- Bhagavan said, Im not putting that in your head. Im not creating this sense of agency, nor am I creating any actions. In other words, the Lord of my being is beyond the world of activity.
And we know this world of activity -- at the Prakriti level. Activity is taking place at the level of Prakriti, this world of plurality, the world where I exist and you exist and the world exists. For any activity to take place, you need two things.
When there is an actor and an object of activity, then only does activity take place. If there is no duality, no activity takes place. Thats why when you are alone, you get bored. By myself, what can I do? I need somebody to play with. Thats why solitude is so difficult for us to practice.
We want a life where everything is going on. But Bhagavan said, in reality there is no duality when it comes down to the core of your being -- yourself, myself, his self, and her self are one. So at that level, no activity is ever taking place. Therefore he says, I am beyond this activity. I am not creating doership, and I am not creating actions.
We constantly blame Bhagavan for things not going right for us. When things go right, I put all the efforts and got it. When things go wrong, Bhagavan is not looking after me these days. He said, I am completely away from your activity. I am not in the business of marrying your actions with the fruits of actions.
Im not taking stock about what Papa I had done or Punya I had done. Its entirely up to you and the world youre working in to figure out the transactions and what is the results of the transactions. Because I created this Prakriti out of my own self by my Maya. In the previous chapter we have seen it clearly stated that I am working in this world out of my own Maya. Ajopi san avyayatma bhutanam ishwaropi san prakritim swam adhishthaya sambhavami atma-mayaya -- by my own Maya, by presiding over this Prakriti, I work in this world.
So once I created the Prakriti out of my own Maya from the Bhagavans perspective, my work is done. I created the field of activity, the rules of the activity, the laws of nature. And we had been saying many, many times in this discussion that the laws of nature are without any exception. They apply to all of us in the Prakriti equally. It does not see that because I have done this many punyas that my papa gets wiped out. Its not a canceling each other type of activity.
You do one good, youre forgiven one bad? No. You pay for your bad and you get reward for your good. Thats the rules of the game. So, one, I am a part of the Prakriti. Im going through my life within the laws of the Prakriti. As long as I am abiding by the rules of the Prakriti, Ill be evolving in the Prakriti.
The whole game -- the Bhagavant Leela, Krishna Leela as we call it -- starts out with being the ignorant self, not knowing who I am. Thats the original sin. When I forgot who I am, that is the original sin -- Avidya. From that Avidya, through my own evolutionary efforts, I evolve. When I was just a single-cell amoeba, I evolved at the lap of Mother Nature. Then I became a human being.
And now I have to evolve with my own efforts. With this evolution, I have to get out of this identification with this body, mind and intellect to identify with the self where the game started when the Avidya started. And I have to get out of the Avidya and become Vidya again. While Im at the Prakriti level, I still have a responsibility and activity to Perform. So in chapter three, we are given the rules of the game. If you really want to evolve in this Prakriti act for the greater good.
All your activities must be for the greater good -- for the Yajna spirit, not for you as this self, this body, mind, and intellect, but for the greater good. By acting for this greater good, I will rise above this selfish ego and purify my mind and intellect. Now, we have been given free will. And therefore, at times we will be acting in line with Dharma, and at times against Dharma. This chapter says, I am not taking any part in your activity.
Its done as per the rules of the games. When I put the key in the ignition of my car, there is no discrimination for BMW to decide whether Im a nice guy or a bad guy, whether Im the owner of the car or the thief who is stealing this BMW. It would work exactly as the laws of thermodynamics and electricity are in this nature. It will start the car as long as I have the right key. So you see, if hes not taking part, then who is maintaining the laws in this nature? If there are laws in this nature, there got to be law giver and law enforcer.
Without a law enforcer, no law is of any value. Because there is law enforcement, the laws are abided by. In this country or anywhere else in this world, we see the laws are very precisely followed in nature. So there has got to be a law enforcer. And if he says Im not taking part, who is enforcing the law? Bhagavan says, thats also me.
As part of my lower nature as a Prakriti, I control the laws of Prakriti. And therefore anytime in a society when majority of the people are not following these laws, I have to take charge again and set those rules visible again for everybody, clarify the situation and make those laws again visible to people to follow. So all the bad elements are weeded out. Dharma is re established. His job as a law enforcer is to make sure that in the Prakriti laws are followed. And therefore Prakriti continues to function as it is designed.
Prakriti is a self regulating entity and therefore Prakriti itself will create its own enforcement and clarification. The verse we saw in chapter four seems like a direct contradiction to this verse. It says whenever there is a decay of Dharma -- but actually Dharma itself is not decaying. Rather, people are not following Dharma. When people are not following Dharma, then yadaa yadaa hi dharmasya glaanir bhavati... tadatmanam srijamy aham -- I manifest myself to get rid of the Adharma, to restore those who are not following Dharma.
So how does that work? Its not at an individual level. Bhagavan doesnt come down and say, Youre a bad guy, Im going to eliminate you. Youre a good guy, Im going to help you. Its like the federal government.
We have this Federal Reserve Bank. This sets the monetary policy. They dont come and call me and say, Rajan, so whats happening in your company? You think you need some help? Can we do something with the interest rate so NBG architecture can function better? Or let me call you a next door guy, whether hes doing okay.
What they look at is the country. Are we doing well as a country? Well, then I dont have to do much -- raise the interest rate, whatever is appropriate. Were not doing well? They have to come down and say, were going to lower the interest rates. And at one point it was practically zero or something like that.
But its not at an individual level. At the national level, at the global level, Bhagavan said, I see -- Yada yada hi Dharmasya glanir bhavati. When I see that overall the Dharma is decaying -- take the green building movement. We saw that Dharma is decaying on this planet. We are constantly emitting carbon dioxide. We are depleting the ozone layer.
So Bhagavan manifests himself through organizations like USGBC, the United States Green Building Council. Now there is an awareness that we need to be working towards sustainable energy, sustainable design, preserving this planet. Anytime theres a decay of Dharma in this global society, this awareness gets created again to reestablish Dharma. But at the individual level, my actions and the rewards of my actions are determined by the nature of my actions, the nature of this world, and the nature of the field in which I act. At that level I have to rely on the laws of society, the laws of nature, laws of the community.

Verse 16 uses the powerful image of the sun: Surely wisdom is like the sun, revealing the supreme truth. Just as the sun does not create light but simply is light, wisdom does not create the Self but reveals what was always present, hidden by ignorance. Verse 17 describes those who meditate on the Divine going whence there is no return - their sins dissolved in wisdom. Most remarkably, verse 18 declares that sages look equally upon all - whether a learned Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, or an outcaste. This sama-darshana (equal vision) is the hallmark of realization.
Today, practice sama-darshana consciously. As you encounter different people - colleagues, service workers, family members, strangers - can you perceive the same consciousness animating each form? The verse deliberately contrasts extremes: the highest (learned Brahmin) with the lowest (outcaste), the large (elephant) with the small (dog). This is not about ignoring differences at the practical level but about recognizing the same Self wearing different costumes. When someone irritates you today, pause and remember: the same awareness that looks out through your eyes is looking out through theirs. When you admire someone, remember: that same light shines in the person you find difficult. This practice of equal seeing is not sentimental but precise - it targets the root of our judgments and preferences. Can you maintain this vision for even five minutes continuously?
